text:
Lia Wang: seeing a big spike in 503s from auth-service since ~14:03 UTC, multiple clients reporting 401/403s after token verification fails
Sam Ortiz: yep, logs show introspect handler returning 503s, upstream jwks fetch failing with 504 from key-sync microservice
Sam Ortiz: example curl from prod-gateway: `curl -I https://auth.redwood.dev/introspect -H \"Authorization: Bearer <tok>\"` -> `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`
Ben Kline: rolling key-sync job started at 13:57, it pushed new signing metadata to vault and triggered sync to auth nodes
Maya (CS Ops): getting multiple CS tickets — customers seeing immediate 401s on generation and embeddings routes, some are in-flight jobs failing :frowning:
Lia Wang: I think the new signing metadata changed `iss` claim shape, validators rejecting tokens issued with the old claim format
Ben Kline: can we temporarily stop the sync and fallback to previous metadata? planning to suspend cronjob
Ben Kline:
```
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob signing-key-sync -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```
Sam Ortiz: doing that now, patching -> ok cronjob suspended
DevOps Bot: [k8s] cronjob signing-key-sync patched by sam. replicas: n/a
Sam Ortiz: restarting auth-service pods with previous config (pointing to `issuer:v2026-02-18`) to pick up old metadata
Lia Wang: also flushing introspect cache on redis to ensure old keys are used until we verify metadata
Sam Ortiz:
```
redis-cli -h redis-prod lrange auth:issuer_cache 0 -1
redis-cli -h redis-prod del auth:issuer_cache
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-service -n platform
```
Maya (CS Ops): notified top 5 impacted customers via status page and PM channels, added them to incident thread, triage ticket created
Ben Kline: after restart a subset of pods still returning 503 for a few minutes while they warm the JWKS cache, but error rate dropping from 12% -> 1% in last 8m :thumbsup:
Lia Wang: full mitigation seems to be working, keeping incident open for 30m to ensure stability. we'll collect traces and request IDs for postmortem
Sam Ortiz: opened incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.dev/INC-2026-045 (fields populated, initial timeline)
Maya (CS Ops): CS asked for rollback detail and ETA for full service recovery, shared current mitigation steps and ETA ~20-30m
Ben Kline: root likely a schema change in the new metadata that key-sync pushed; will disable the new publisher until change merged and we'll add stronger validation in the sync job
Lia Wang: thanks all — followups: (1) postmortem, (2) add unit test for issuer shape in key-sync, (3) add canary job before global publish. closing when stable :white_check_mark:
